title: The Archer's Wager
text: A one-eyed archer sits at a crossroads, fletching arrows from feathers nobody has seen on a living bird. He offers a contest against his target, a straw man stuck full of shafts. Whoever misses it the most, he says, may have lessons.

options.label: The one with the poorest eye takes his lessons, swallowing their pride.

outcomes.text: By dusk they are hitting the straw man without looking. The archer will not say who taught him, or what became of them.

options.label: The sharpest eye takes up his contest, sure of their aim.

outcomes.text: They win. The archer pays in arrows of a strange, dark make, fletched with those unknown feathers.
The old archer wins without even looking. His laughter follows you long after you have gone.

options.label: Take his quiver while he sleeps. A one-eyed man sees only half of what goes on.

outcomes.text: The archer stirs and swiftly looses an arrow, which finds the thief's arm with precision.
You escape with a full quiver. His curses follow, so specific that you feel them settle on your shoulders.
